overview: This Senate resolution states the Senate's view that Samuel Bankman-Fried, co-founder of the collapsed cryptocurrency exchange FTX, should never receive a presidential pardon, a shortened sentence or any other form of clemency. It recounts his 2023 conviction by a federal jury on seven fraud and conspiracy counts and his 25-year prison sentence, and notes that he has applied for a pardon. It affirms that the sentence serves justice, rejects calling his prosecution politically motivated, and restates support for protecting investors and the integrity of U.S. financial markets. As a 'sense of the Senate' resolution, it expresses an opinion and does not limit the President's pardon power. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on July 15, 2026.
for: Supporters say it sends a clear message that large-scale financial fraud will be punished and stands up for the many customers who lost money.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic, cannot restrict the President's constitutional pardon power, and singles out one person's pending clemency request.
